positions.as_written: Use a cartilage sensitive sequence and look specifically at the deep interface rather than the surface.
Assess the surface separately, since it is characteristically intact.
Assess the subchondral marrow, which is usually abnormal beneath it.
Confirm in a second plane, because a line at an interface is exactly what partial volume averaging produces.
The subchondral marrow responds to that altered load, which is why marrow signal beneath an intact surface should prompt a look at the interface.
